faq.a: Khasan is associated with the Arabic form حَسَن, whose core sense is khasan; good, handsome (caucasian form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Khasan?
faq.a: Khasan is associated with Arabic. Khasan is the Caucasian form of Arabic حَسَن (Ḥasan), meaning 'good, handsome'.
Yes — the underlying form حَسَن is Arabic.
Khasan can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Khasan should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ح س ن is Quranic, but Ḥasan is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: In Urdu, Khasan is rendered حسن and carries the sense حسن، اچھا.

faq.q: What does Khasan mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Khasan is rendered حسن and carries the sense حسن، نیکو.
A romanized syllable approximation is kha-san. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Khasan?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Khasan, khasan. Script forms are حسن, حَسَن, ख़सन.

faq.q: Is Khasan a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
